key_concepts: Stems support plants, transport water and nutrients, and sometimes photosynthesize.
Roots anchor plants, absorb water and minerals, and may store food.
Leaves carry out photosynthesis, gas exchange, and sometimes water retention.

Rhizomes are horizontal underground stems that store nutrients and enable vegetative repro
Tubers are enlarged stem parts that store nutrients and are not roots.
Thorns are sharp hardened structures that protect plants from herbivores.
Bulbs are short stems with fleshy leaves that store food during dormancy and support regro
Aerial roots grow above ground and absorb moisture and nutrients from the air.
Aerial roots are common in humid tropical or swampy habitats, such as orchids.
